subject: Re: ACME Private Deployment — VPC Forwarder & SIEM Handoff
messages:
From: Paul Evans <paul.evans@acme-corp.com>

Cc: security@acme-corp.com, timothy.li@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME: Private deployment — observability export options

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving toward a private deployment in our AWS VPC for PHI workloads and need to lock down how observability will be exported to our Splunk instance (hosted on-prem behind our firewall). A few constraints from our security team:

- No outbound internet egress from the enclave except to whitelisted vendor IPs.
- All telemetry must be signed and have integrity checks; tokens rotate monthly.
- Trace and metric pipelines must support OTLP (gRPC) or Zipkin; logs should be forwarded via TLS syslog or Splunk HEC.
- PII must be redacted at source where feasible; hashed identifiers are acceptable.

Questions: can Redwood's forwarder run inside our VPC, authenticate to our Splunk HEC with mTLS, and support token rotation without manual ops? If not, what alternate patterns (S3 presigned, VPN pull, peering) do you recommend?

Please include a short checklist for our infra team (ports, firewall rules, expected IP ranges) and a plan for a test window.

Regards,
Paul Evans
Infra Eng Manager
Acme Corp
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Paul Evans <paul.evans@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME: Private deployment — observability export options

Paul — thanks for the clear constraints. Short answer: yes, we support a customer-hosted forwarder pattern that meets your requirements and also have a VPN/peering option if you prefer inbound pull. High-level options (we'll pick one in the tech review):

1) Customer-hosted forwarder (recommended):
   - Deploy Redwood edge-forwarder as a container/VM in your VPC.
   - It posts telemetry to your Splunk HEC over mTLS / TLS with client certs you provision.
   - Supports automated token rotation via API + short-lived certs; we can integrate with your KMS for cert retrieval if allowed.

2) S3 presigned upload (no persistent connection):
   - Forwarder writes compressed batches to an S3 bucket you control using presigned PUTs.
   - Your SIEM pulls from S3 on your schedule. Lower real-time guarantees but works in strict egress-blocking setups.

3) Redwoods pull via site-to-site VPN:
   - You expose an internal HEC endpoint over the VPN; our collector pulls. Requires network setup but removes outbound internet from the enclave.

I'll get Marissa and Karthik to draft a one-page checklist (ports, IPs, token lifecycle, sampling guidance). Can we book a 60-minute tech review Friday 11:00 AM PT?

- Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, Paul Evans <paul.evans@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: ACME: Private deployment — observability export options

Paul — adding technical details to help your security team evaluate. Quoting your constraints below then recommended specifics.

> All telemetry must be signed and have integrity checks; tokens rotate monthly.

- Authentication: we support mTLS for HEC and client cert rotation using ACME or your internal CA. For token-based HEC, we recommend short-lived tokens (7d) in combination with a rotating service-account token. Redwood's forwarder can fetch rotated tokens from an API endpoint you expose or read from a Secrets Manager via an IAM role.

> Trace and metric pipelines must support OTLP (gRPC) or Zipkin; logs should be forwarded via TLS syslog or Splunk HEC.

- Protocols: forwarder supports OTLP/gRPC for traces and metrics and can forward logs via TLS syslog or Splunk HEC (HEC over 8088/443). We also support protobuf compression for OTLP to reduce bandwidth.

> PII must be redacted at source...

- Redaction: recommend running Vector or Fluent Bit preprocessor with regex-based redaction + hashing for identifiers. We provide a filter module in the forwarder to apply your redaction rules; we can supply a default redact-regex file for review.

Firewall / network checklist (minimal):
- Allow outbound 443, 8088 to your Splunk HEC IPs if using HEC over TLS.
- Allow outbound 4317 (gRPC) for OTLP if using gRPC endpoints.
- If using site-to-site VPN, allow internal CIDR peering and NAT rules for the forwarder.
- If using S3 presigned uploads, allow HTTPS to the S3 endpoint(s) you provide.

Test plan:
- Day 0: deploy forwarder in staging VPC with test certs/tokens.
- Day 1: send synthetic traces/logs, validate integrity headers and redaction.
- Day 2: run token rotation and verify no loss.
- Day 3: run load at 2x baseline and ensure batching behavior meets latency SLOs.

I'll attach a short checklist and a network diagram. Happy to walk through Friday.

--
Karthik Iyer
Infra Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of clarifications before the call:

- Can the forwarder be run as a DaemonSet in our EKS cluster (we prefer Kubernetes native patterns)?
- For mTLS, we prefer that Redwood not hold any private keys. Can your rotation work with our KMS (AWS KMS) so private keys never leave our account?
- For audit, we need an evidence bundle (signed manifest) after each rotation window.

Attachments: please send the checklist and the diagram you mentioned. We'll validate and provide open firewall windows for the scheduled test.

Paul

Paul — quick summary and next steps (action owner in parens):

1) Deployment model: run Redwood edge-forwarder as a DaemonSet in your EKS cluster (preferred). We will provide a Helm chart and example manifests. (Action: Karthik / Redwood)
2) mTLS & key custody: support for AWS KMS integration so private keys remain in your account; Redwood only receives a CSR-signed client cert or short-lived token. (Action: Paul / Acme + Redwood security)
3) Redaction & PII: use our preprocessor filter (Vector-based) for regex hashing; provide default rule-set for review. (Action: Acme security to provide sample logs; Hannah to review rules)
4) Network checklist: allow egress to Splunk HEC IPs on 443/8088; if you prefer no egress, we will schedule site-to-site VPN setup. (Action: Acme infra)
5) Test window: propose Wed 16 Jun 2027 9:00 AM PT for staging validation. We'll need a test HEC endpoint, test certs/tokens, and a staging namespace in your EKS. (Action: Paul to confirm)
6) Deliverables before test: architecture diagram (attached), SIEM deployment checklist (attached), sample helm chart, and token rotation runbook link. (Action: Vanessa / Marissa)

Attachments: acme-forwarder-architecture-v1.pdf; siem-deployment-checklist.xlsx

If this looks good I'll lock the calendar and create a short Confluence page with the plan and verification steps.
